text.p: Italian bonds and futures ended a colourless session higher on Friday's close but with reduced gains in a fairly directionless market following huge gains seen last week on Italy's budget, traders said.

Weaker bonds had weighed on the market, adding to the uncertainty about which road to follow now. "The mood is still positive but many operators see a downward correction before any new gains," one trader said.
The dollar was consolidating around 991 against the mark after touching a new 26-month high of 989.10 but the currency's firmness failed to give much of a boost.
"The Italian economy continues to offer good fundamentals but players want a pause for reflection," one primary dealer said. Some profit-taking emerged on Btp gains "also to adjust long positions."

The spread over 10-year bunds came in slightly to a late 232 basis points from an early 234. In the cash market, the Feb 2006 gross yield was up a touch at 8.31 pct. "The 10-year is coming out of a period of high volatility. For the future I see limited fluctuations in an 8.25-8.50 range," the dealer said.
"High-yielders have had a good run. Now it could be the moment for core paper like bunds and T-bonds," one trader said.
